summary: Frontend-only verification of the county↔postcode-area geometric bridge fix in CRM → Territories → Map. All 3 scenarios PASS: (1) painting Greater Manchester on the counties layer causes postcode area 'M' to inherit the rep colour on the postcode layer; (2) painting 'B' on the postcode layer causes West Midlands to inherit the rep colour on the counties layer; (3) unrelated regions (ZE postcode, Cornwall county) remain the neutral white fill. Cleanup toggles restored both regions to neutral. PUT /api/crm/territories/region/... returned 200 for all paint operations.

test_evidence.postcode_M_after_county_paint: fill rgb(37,99,235) — INHERITED from county via bridge (bug fix confirmed)
test_evidence.county_WestMidlands_after_B_paint: fill rgb(37,99,235) — INHERITED from postcode area B via bridge (reverse direction confirmed)
test_evidence.network: PUT /api/crm/territories/region/county/Greater%20Manchester -> 200; PUT /api/crm/territories/region/postcode_area/B -> 200; both paint and unpaint (toggle) PUTs observed

critical_code_review_comments: CRMTerritoryMap.js is 915 lines — consider splitting rendering / palette / bridge computation into smaller modules for maintainability.

SVG Geography onClick is not reliable via Playwright .click(force=True); native pointer events must be dispatched. Consider adding a wrapping <rect pointer-events='fill'> or exposing an accessible handler to make E2E testing more robust (not a functional bug).
Suggest exposing effective vs direct coverage counts in the 'Painting: X · N counties' pill to communicate the bridge behaviour to end users.
seed_data_creation: None; painted Greater Manchester (county) and B (postcode area) with Demo Manager A, then toggled both OFF to restore original state as instructed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Territory Map bridge fix verified. To repaint via Playwright, dispatch native pointerdown/mousedown/pointerup/mouseup/click on the SVG Geography (page.click force=True does not trigger react-simple-maps onClick reliably).
